text:
Alex: Heads-up — saw two tenants today where primary model (r8-large) hit saturated queue for ~40s and requests automatically fell back to r8-quant at the cluster boundary. Quality complaints from CS already.
Priya: ugh. Which clusters/regions? any particular tenant tiers?
Alex: us-west1 pool A, both are mid-enterprise (tier: standard). looks like autoscale didn't spin up fast enough and router demoted to compatible quant variant.
Maya: customer reported hallucination increase after fallback. they're on a predictable SLA, so this is bad.
Caleb: is fallback policy currently: "allow fallback if capacity_exceeded" with no tenant-tier override?
Emile: yeah, router has simple eq: if queue_len > threshold OR cpu_util > 0.92 -> route to compatible_variants ordered by cost. it's intentionally aggressive to avoid 503s.
Alex: proposal: introduce per-tenant fallback policy + console toggle to prefer "try-primary-only" for SLA customers (fail closed instead of degrade quality).
Priya: we also need to track metrics to know when fallback happens and impact. suggest these new telemetry events: `fallback.triggered`, `fallback.variant`, `fallback.reason`, linked to request_id and tenant_id.
Caleb: Product + Sales will want a UI that shows how often fallback triggers and the cost/latency tradeoff. a small dashboard tile.
Maya: also need automated alerts when fallback rate > X% for a tenant over a 5m window. our CSMs need heads-up before customers notice.
Emile: agree. ops design: what about adding a header that callers can set: `Prefer-Primary: true|false|best-effort` so customers can opt-in programmatically?
Alex: good idea. header semantics: `Prefer-Primary: strict` => route only to pinned primary, return 503 if not possible; `best-effort` => current behavior.
Priya: caveat: strict may increase 5xxs during global outages. need per-tenant fallback policy with safety cap for platform health. e.g., global kill-switch on console and an emergency override that still falls back if queue_len > critical_max to keep cluster alive.
Caleb: UX: in the console per-tenant settings page add a section "Fallback behavior" with three radio options: Strict (return error), Conservative (try primary, then compatible within same tier), Aggressive (any compatible variant). Show estimated cost delta and expected quality risk.
Alex: code sketch for policy JSON we could use in API:

```
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-123",
  "fallback_policy": {
    "mode": "conservative",
    "max_fallback_rate": 0.1,
    "same_region_only": true,
    "sticky_duration_sec": 300
  }
}
```

Emile: sticky_duration_sec is important — don't oscillate per-request. but sticky should respect autoscaling events.
Priya: telemetry naming nit: use `router.fallback.*` to align with other router metrics. and emit `router.fallback.sampling_quality_loss` when we have golden-reference checks.
Maya: can we do sampled golden checks? like 1% of fallbacked requests get checked against primary later to measure divergence. that'd quantify impact.
Alex: yes. add a `fallback_probe` flow which replays user input to primary in low-priority background path and logs logits/diffs.
Caleb: rollout plan: feature-flag the console toggle and header support. start with internal tenants + a small canary group. show new dashboard in Canary org for two weeks.
Emile: runtime changes: need router to consult tenant policy store synchronously (cache TTL 5s). also route decision needs to prefer regional matching variant if same_region_only. implement fast-path cache to avoid extra latency in hot path.
Priya: SRE asks: what about QPS scanning cost of replay probes? must be throttled and soft-throttled by tenant.
Alex: probes to be limited to 0.1 RPS per tenant by default, configurable.
Maya: when we surface this in support playbook, call it "Fallback Behavior" and include recommended defaults for enterprise vs standard.
Caleb: also add a metric for "fallback.quality_regressions" tied to customer tickets to close feedback loop.
Emile: ops/implementation note: router config change will need migration script to set existing tenants to default `mode=aggressive` to preserve behavior unless they opt-in.
Priya: can we also add a console wide toggle: "Platform-managed emergency fallback" that ops can flip during large-scale scale-up incidents to prevent total cluster collapse?
Alex: yep — emergency toggle + per-tenant policy + header. good coverage.
Maya: do we have a plan for customer communication? Sales needs templated language explaining tradeoffs and how to set `Prefer-Primary` headers.
Caleb: I'll draft docs and console help text.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: flag/router-fallback-policy-v1 -> staging
Emile: I'll land runtime PR with cache + header parsing into staging, then route to canary.
Priya: SRE will add the `router.fallback.*` metrics to prometheus and create alert: `rate(router.fallback.count[5m]) by (tenant) > 0.05` -> page on slack-alerts.
Alex: Action items: Caleb -> docs + console copy, Emile -> runtime + cache + probe flow, Priya -> metrics + alerts, Maya -> support playbook, Alex -> console toggle mockups. can we ship canary next Tuesday?
Caleb: tentative yes, depends on Emile's PR.
Maya: I'll prep CS comms once we have canary results.
Alex: thanks all. leaving a small test snippet for QA: `curl -H "Prefer-Primary: strict" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — should 503 when primary unavailable.
ops-bot: alert: router queue length spike detected us-west1 pool A 10:34:12 — fallback_rate 0.28 for tenant acme-123
Priya: noted, investigating scaling logs now.
Emile: will follow up with PR link and staging run results.
Alex: closing thread for now, will open follow-ups for console mockups and design doc. :thumbsup:
